title: derive.py measures no 14-day rework: the cloud clone is shallow
problem: `derive.py report` shows 'rework measured 0' for every track and version on 11,280 records, so reviews compare versions on success and merge rate alone; the rework, revert and 14-day survival columns that measure whether work lasted are always empty.
evidence: review 2026-11-28 (E128): `derive.py report` after `fetch --limit 300 && build`: rework measured 0 on every row; coverage table 'rework | 0 | 0 (window closed)'

prompts/derived/runs.json 2026-11-28: rework window 'unavailable' with why "landing commit not on this clone's branch" on 5,367 rows, 'no local branch for .../oss-research-monorepo' on 165, 'open' (under 14 days) on 300; `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` is true
change: Have `build` deepen only as far as the oldest merge in the 14-day window (`git fetch --shallow-since=<date> origin main`) before computing rework, or compute rework from the GitHub API commit list instead of local git; say in the report when history was missing rather than printing 0.
metric: rows with rework measured > 0 in `derive.py report` at the next review
